messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Elevated KV cache paging on dedicated-pool-3 for model llama-awq-7b. paging_ratio=0.87 (6m sustained). Auto-throttle engaged. Incident ID: INC-20260315-001

eric: I'm oncall — looking at the dashboards. Sharp jump in kv_size after the canary rollout ~1802504189. Continuous_batcher is thrashing, causing tail latency spikes and some 5xxs from the pool.

julia: Confirming from metrics: per-node kv_size went from ~1.2GB -> 5.8GB after the quant-path change. Traces show kernel selection "awq-int8-attn" for attention_kv_store. OOM eviction events spiked.

anais: Which rollout triggered this? Who approved the AWQ quant change?

lin: Canary: model 'llama-awq-7b:v2026-03-15' was pushed to dedicated-pool-3 as an automated canary at 1802504189. That build enabled AWQ packing + kernel autotune.

sam: Customer impact: two customers reported >30s timeouts and automated retries. CS reported 3 active tickets.

eric: Quick mitigation plan (live):
1) Route traffic off AWQ quant path -> fallback gptq variant for the dedicated pool.
2) Lower continuous_batch_target from 64 -> 8 to reduce batch memory pressure.
3) Disable prefix KV caching for the affected model.
4) Apply attention kernel fallback to fp16 for AWQ path as stopgap.

anais: Assigning tasks: @eric do the routing cut, @lin disable prefix caching, @julia monitor KV evictions & paging, @sam coordinate customer comms.

eric: Starting routing rollback now.
deploy-bot: job job-78021 started: routing update for model=llama-awq-7b -> target=gptq-7b (scope: dedicated-pool-3).

eric: Command I executed:
```
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.internal/api/v1/routes" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"llama-awq-7b","target":"gptq-7b","weight":1.0,"scope":"dedicated-pool-3"}'
```

lin: Disabling prefix caching config for model:
```
rdctl model update --model llama-awq-7b \ 
  --config '{"cache":{"prefix_caching":false}}' --scope dedicated-pool-3
```
Done on 6/6 nodes — update converging.

julia: Quick metrics after the changes: paging_ratio 0.87 -> 0.35 within 90s, average per-node kv_size -> 1.4GB. Latency tail improved but still above SLO for ~2m while caches settle.

customer-support: Notified affected customers. Tickets: #CS-4451, #CS-4453. Message sent: "Mitigation applied; we are routing you to fallback models to restore latency. RCA to follow."

eric: Also lowered continuous batching for the pool:
```
rdctl cluster update --pool dedicated-pool-3 --continuous_batch_target 8
```
Batch queue depth dropped and CPU/mem pressure reduced.

julia: Observed logs (eviction summary):
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] node-3: KV_EVICT count=47, kv_pages=15243 -> 4821, mem_free_increase=3.2GB
[2026-03-15T12:03:49Z] node-1: paging_event count=12, latency_spike p99=5.2s
```

julia: Preliminary root cause: AWQ quant path changed internal KV layout (per-head packing/alignment), increasing per-entry metadata and causing 3-5x KV footprint on some sequence shapes. Kernel autotune selected awq-int8 attention kernel which stores denser but larger-aligned pages. Under heavy tail, the extra footprint caused cache blowup and paging.

anais: Do we have a perf/regression test that would catch this kv_size delta?

lin: Not yet. Action: add an integration perf test that switches quant backend between awq/gptq/gptq-int8 and asserts kv_size delta < 2x for typical workloads. Also add an automatic kernel fallback if kv_size > threshold within 5m.

sam: For customers: we'll include mitigation details and ETA for RCA. Suggest sending interim update in 60–120 minutes.

eric: I'm pinning dedicated-pool-3 routing to gptq-7b until we have a patched AWQ kernel or a KV-footprint guard. Opening follow-up PR to disable AWQ kernel autotune on dedicated pools.

deploy-bot: job job-78021 completed: success on 6/6 nodes. Rollback done.

julia: Confirming steady-state at +10m: paging_ratio 0.12, kv_size stable ~1.1GB, no new OOM/evictions in last 10m. Latency back within SLO for most customers; two customers still seeing retries, CS following up.

customer-support: Update posted to tickets: "Mitigation applied; we've routed your traffic to an alternative model and are investigating root cause. We'll send full RCA within 24 hours." :thumbsup:

anais: Good mitigation. Postmortem action items: add perf tests, add kernel-fallback policy, add alert for kv_size delta > 2x, and review rollout gating for quant path changes.

eric: Oncall handoff: I'll remain available for 30 more minutes, then hand to @julia. Adding note to oncall board and to the incident tracker INC-20260315-001.

julia: Acknowledged. I'll monitor for 3 hours and start drafting RCA with runtime + infra.

eric: Closing loop: root-cause owner = runtime/eng-ml (julia/lin), mitigation owner = infra (eric), customer comms = sam.

anais: Thanks team. :clap:
